minutes.headline: Sewer Commission re-elected its officers, adopted a new oil-water separator log, and began an emergency pump-failure response plan.
minutes.summary: The commission elected a chair, vice chair and clerk, approved the minutes, and voted to accept a new oil/water separator inspection and maintenance log for property owners. Staff presented an emergency response plan prompted by two pump failures at the Dana Street station, and updated the board on Leominster/Fitchburg IMA rate increases and ARPA funding for manholes. The meeting adjourned after a roll call.

public_comment.topic: A commissioner/speaker offered condolences to Jane and sympathy for flood victims, and promoted the next day's volunteer/retirement fair at the adult activity center. (Speaker appears to be a board member; no public attended.)

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the 8/29 meeting
Accept the new oil/water separator inspection and maintenance log form

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff said connection charges will need to rise if Leominster's proposed hookup charge goes ahead.
Staff circulated a worksheet modelling the effect of Fitchburg and Leominster rate increases on income and operating costs and on homeowners and businesses.
The town allocated money for manhole repairs, which will go out through an IFB; timing of the funds was not yet confirmed.
The commission had asked the town for pump station money that was largely not granted; staff said capital planning is needed and will affect rates.

budget_items.topic: Vacuum pump, spare pump and rebuild kits
budget_items.what_was_said: Cost of the new vacuum pump, spare pump and rebuilds at six stations was called substantial; invoice to be submitted.

decisions.decision: Staff to go ahead and develop the bid (IFB/RFP) for manhole repairs; no vote needed.
Emergency response plan stays on the agenda until complete; final draft to go to department heads and other agencies, with Board of Health and water district added.
Next meeting on the 26th; emergency response plan and the IMA to remain on agendas; no meeting at month end around Halloween.
Commissioners to send IMA comments only to Paula, who will compile them for the negotiating team.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to accept a new oil/water separator inspection and maintenance log form for property owners; the motion passed.
Staff presented an emergency response plan for pump station failures; it stays on the agenda until a final draft goes to department heads and other agencies.
Staff updated the board on Leominster and Fitchburg rate increases and a possible hookup charge, and circulated a worksheet modelling the effect on income, costs and customers.
Staff were told to go ahead and develop a bid for manhole repairs paid from town ARPA money, with no vote needed; timing of the funds was not confirmed.
Roll-call votes elected a chair, vice chair and clerk, but the captions do not make the outcomes audible.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates and connection charges can rise because Leominster and Fitchburg raise what they charge the town, and staff said local connection charges would need to rise if Leominster's hookup charge goes ahead.
The commission asked the town for pump station money that was largely not granted, so future capital needs are likely to be paid through sewer rates rather than other town funds.
Property owners with oil/water separators, such as businesses, now have a standard inspection and maintenance log form to use.
watch_next: Next meeting on the 26th: the emergency response plan and the Leominster/Fitchburg IMA stay on the agenda.
The bid for manhole repairs, once staff develop it and the ARPA funds are confirmed.
